headline: Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam faced with attempted murder case
summary: The MP was accused of attempting to kill his own driver by strangulation over a dispute regarding an immoral relationship and a leaked video.
details: A case has been filed against Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and four others at the Pallabi Police Station in Dhaka.
The case was filed by the driver of the MP's personal car, Obaidur Rahman, who alleged that he was beaten and strangled in an attempt to kill him.
The allegations stem from a dispute over an 'immoral relationship' and the suspected leak of a video.
Among the accused, one individual named Aminur Rahman has already been arrested and sent to jail by a court.
Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin ordered the investigation and directed that a report be submitted by August 28.
Separately, Jamaat-e-Islami has expelled the MP from the party over 'moral misconduct', and the Election Commission has stated it will take action according to the law.
caption:
An MP's driver claims he was strangled in an attempt to kill him over a leaked video. Now, the lawmaker is facing a serious criminal case.

A case has been filed against Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and four others at the Pallabi Police Station in Dhaka.

The case was filed by the driver of the MP's personal car, Obaidur Rahman, who alleged that he was beaten and strangled in an attempt to kill him.

The allegations stem from a dispute over an 'immoral relationship' and the suspected leak of a video.

Among the accused, one individual named Aminur Rahman has already been arrested and sent to jail by a court.

Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin ordered the investigation and directed that a report be submitted by August 28.

Separately, Jamaat-e-Islami has expelled the MP from the party over 'moral misconduct', and the Election Commission has stated it will take action according to the law.

#Bangladesh #Satkhira #Politics #CrimeNews #Lawmaker

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Union Parishad [[elections to be held early next year]], says Minister
headline: Union Parishad elections to be held early next year, says Minister
summary: Local Government Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir promises a completely neutral election process without favoritism toward any party.
details: Local Government Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced that Union Parishad elections will take place in the early part of next year.
Speaking at a discussion meeting organized by the Bangladesh Union Chairman-Member Association in Kakrail, Dhaka, he emphasized that the elections will be completely neutral.
The Minister stated that no political party, including the BNP or Jamaat-e-Islami, would receive any unfair advantage in the process.
He urged candidates for Chairman, Member, and female members to win based on the popularity and love of the people, calling it the foundation of democracy.
Minister Fakhrul also warned against the politics of division based on religion, stating that while the majority believe in Islam, respect must be shown to all faiths.
He noted that religion is personal, but the state belongs to everyone, and cautioned against using religion to create divisions within society.
He further argued that strong local government is essential for a strong democracy and the что the previous administration under the Awami League had destroyed democracy.
The Minister concluded by claiming that the Awami League had looted and forced their way through elections, failing to maintain democratic principles.
caption:
Union Parishad elections are coming early next year. The Minister promises a completely neutral process.

Local Government Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced that Union Parishad elections will take place in the early part of next year.

Speaking at a discussion meeting organized by the Bangladesh Union Chairman-Member Association in Kakrail, Dhaka, he emphasized that the elections will be completely neutral.

The Minister stated that no political party, including the BNP or Jamaat-e-Islami, would receive any unfair advantage in the process.

He urged candidates for Chairman, Member, and female members to win based on the popularity and love of the people, calling it the foundation of democracy.

Minister Fakhrul also warned against the politics of division based on religion, stating that while the majority believe in Islam, respect must be shown to all faiths.

He noted that religion is personal, but the state belongs to everyone, and cautioned against using religion to create divisions within society.

He further argued that strong local government is essential for a strong democracy and the что the previous administration under the Awami League had destroyed democracy.

The Minister concluded by claiming that the Awami League had looted and forced their way through elections, failing to maintain democratic principles.
